name: Context-Changing Transition Permitted
research_question: Does the CSP evaluator determine feasibility based on explicit transition constraints rather than falsely assuming contradiction when request-scoped values differ across a pivot?

produced_context.description: Compromised bastion host establishes an internal VPC origin for subsequent requests

transition_constraints.rationale: Traversal of hop 1 compromises the bastion host, shifting the attacker's request-origin from the external internet to the bastion's VPC IP (10.0.1.100). The transition does not enforce SourceIp(hop1) == SourceIp(hop2).

formal_rationale: Although 198.51.100.0/24 and 10.0.0.0/16 are disjoint CIDR blocks, aws:SourceIp is a request-scoped attribute whose origin mutates across the pivot hop. Hop 1 produces an internal VPC execution context (10.0.1.100). The transition constraint explicitly binds SourceIp(hop2) to this produced context rather than equating it to SourceIp(hop1). The system is fully satisfied by SourceIp(hop1) = 198.51.100.42 and SourceIp(hop2) = 10.0.1.100.
falsification_criteria: The feasibility hypothesis is falsified if the evaluator blindly flags disjoint request-scoped values as a contradiction (returning UNSAT) without evaluating the explicit pivot transition constraints.
